name: Bath
description: A stunning Georgian city built around natural hot springs. Roman Baths, the Royal Crescent, and Jane Austen connections make this one of England's most beautiful cities.

highlights.name: Roman Baths
highlights.description: Remarkably preserved 2,000-year-old Roman bathing complex.

highlights.name: Thermae Bath Spa
highlights.description: Britain's only natural thermal spa. Rooftop pool with city views.

highlights.name: Royal Crescent & The Circus
highlights.description: Iconic Georgian architecture — the finest crescent of townhouses in the UK.

highlights.name: Jane Austen Centre
highlights.description: Explore the life and works of Bath's most famous resident.

highlights.name: Pulteney Bridge & Weir
highlights.description: One of only four bridges in the world lined with shops on both sides.

highlights.name: Sally Lunn's Historic Eating House
highlights.description: The oldest house in Bath (1482). Famous for the original Bath Bun.

name: Edinburgh
description: Scotland's dramatic capital — a UNESCO World Heritage city of castles, cobbled streets, and literary pubs. Stunning architecture split between the medieval Old Town and Georgian New Town.

highlights.name: Edinburgh Castle
highlights.description: Iconic fortress dominating the city skyline from Castle Rock.

highlights.name: Arthur's Seat
highlights.description: Hike the ancient volcano for panoramic city views. 251m summit.

highlights.name: The Royal Mile
highlights.description: A mile of history from the Castle to Holyrood Palace. Closes, wynds, and hidden courtyards.

highlights.name: Scotch Whisky Experience
highlights.description: Learn about Scotland's national drink with tastings and the world's largest Scotch whisky collection.

highlights.name: National Museum of Scotland
highlights.description: World-class museum spanning science, nature, art, and Scottish history. Free entry.

highlights.name: Calton Hill
highlights.description: Sunset viewpoint with neoclassical monuments. The 'Athens of the North'.

name: The Cotswolds
description: Rolling hills, honey-coloured stone villages, and quintessential English countryside. Bibury, Castle Combe, and Bourton-on-the-Water are picture-perfect.

highlights.name: Bibury & Arlington Row
highlights.description: William Morris called it 'the most beautiful village in England'. The row of weavers' cottages is iconic.

highlights.name: Bourton-on-the-Water
highlights.description: The 'Venice of the Cotswolds' — a picture-perfect village with low bridges over the River Windrush.

highlights.name: Stow-on-the-Wold
highlights.description: Charming market town with antique shops and the famous tree-framed church door.

highlights.name: Castle Combe
highlights.description: Regularly voted England's prettiest village. Medieval market cross and golden stone cottages.

highlights.name: Blenheim Palace
highlights.description: Birthplace of Winston Churchill. Magnificent baroque palace with stunning gardens.

highlights.name: Cotswolds Farm Park
highlights.description: Meet rare breed farm animals. Great for families.

name: York
description: A medieval walled city with a Viking heritage, Gothic cathedral, and The Shambles — one of the best-preserved medieval streets in Europe.

highlights.name: York Minster
highlights.description: The largest Gothic cathedral in Northern Europe. Stunning stained glass and climb the tower for views.

highlights.name: The Shambles
highlights.description: A narrow medieval street that inspired Diagon Alley in Harry Potter. Now packed with independent shops.

highlights.name: Jorvik Viking Centre
highlights.description: Travel back to Viking-age York on a ride through a recreated Viking settlement.

highlights.name: York City Walls
highlights.description: Walk the 2-mile medieval walls encircling the city. The best-preserved in England.

highlights.name: York Chocolate Story
highlights.description: York was the chocolate capital of Britain. Interactive tour through the history of Rowntree's, Terry's, and Kit Kat.

highlights.name: Betty's Tea Rooms
highlights.description: A York institution since 1936. Queues out the door for their legendary afternoon tea.

bestPubs: The House of the Trembling Madness

name: Lake District
description: England's most dramatic landscape — mountains, lakes, and literary heritage. Wordsworth's inspiration, Beatrix Potter's home, and some of Britain's finest hiking.

highlights.name: Lake Windermere Cruise
highlights.description: A scenic cruise on England's longest lake. Stunning mountain backdrop.

highlights.name: Catbells Fell Walk
highlights.description: The most popular fell walk in the Lakes. Manageable summit with spectacular Derwentwater views.

highlights.name: Beatrix Potter Gallery & Hill Top
highlights.description: Visit the home where Beatrix Potter wrote her famous tales.

highlights.name: Dove Cottage (Wordsworth)
highlights.description: The poet William Wordsworth's home. Where he wrote his greatest works.

highlights.name: Ambleside & Grasmere
highlights.description: Charming lakeside villages with excellent shops, cafes, and Grasmere gingerbread.

highlights.name: Helvellyn via Striding Edge
highlights.description: One of England's most thrilling mountain walks. Only for experienced hikers.

name: Oxford
description: The City of Dreaming Spires. Home to the world's oldest English-speaking university, with stunning college architecture, Harry Potter film locations, and covered markets.

highlights.name: Bodleian Library & Divinity School
highlights.description: One of Europe's oldest libraries. The Divinity School was used as the Hogwarts infirmary.

highlights.name: Christ Church College
highlights.description: The Great Hall inspired the Hogwarts dining hall. Lewis Carroll was a fellow here.

highlights.name: Radcliffe Camera & All Souls
highlights.description: Oxford's most photographed building. A circular library of extraordinary beauty.

highlights.name: Covered Market
highlights.description: A historic market since 1774 with independent shops, delis, and cafes.

highlights.name: Punting on the Cherwell
highlights.description: Glide along the river in a flat-bottomed punt. A quintessential Oxford experience.

name: Cambridge
description: A beautiful university city of medieval colleges, soaring chapels, and peaceful river meadows. Punting on the Cam is a must.

highlights.name: King's College Chapel
highlights.description: One of the finest examples of Gothic architecture in Europe. The fan-vaulted ceiling is breathtaking.

highlights.name: Punting on the Cam
highlights.description: Punt past the famous 'Backs' — the stunning college gardens that back onto the river.

highlights.name: The Fitzwilliam Museum
highlights.description: World-class art collection in a stunning neoclassical building. Free entry.

highlights.name: The Mathematical Bridge
highlights.description: A famous wooden bridge at Queens' College — legend says it was designed by Newton.

name: Cornwall
description: Dramatic cliffs, turquoise seas, and charming fishing villages. St Ives, Padstow, and the Eden Project make Cornwall feel like another country entirely.

highlights.name: St Ives
highlights.description: An artists' paradise with golden beaches, the Tate St Ives gallery, and cobbled streets. Cornwall's prettiest town.

highlights.name: Eden Project
highlights.description: Giant biomes housing the world's largest indoor rainforest. Architecture as spectacular as the plants.

highlights.name: Padstow & Rick Stein
highlights.description: A foodie fishing village made famous by chef Rick Stein. Incredible seafood.

highlights.name: Minack Theatre
highlights.description: An open-air theatre carved into a cliff above the sea. Performances with the Atlantic as backdrop.

highlights.name: St Michael's Mount
highlights.description: A fairytale castle on a tidal island. Walk across the causeway at low tide.

highlights.name: Coastal Path Walking
highlights.description: Part of the 630-mile South West Coast Path. Dramatic cliff walks with wildflowers and seabirds.

name: Liverpool
description: UNESCO World Heritage waterfront, the Beatles, two cathedrals, and one of the UK's best food and nightlife scenes. A city of culture, music, and football.

highlights.name: The Beatles Story
highlights.description: The world's largest permanent Beatles exhibition at the Albert Dock.

highlights.name: Anfield Stadium Tour (Liverpool FC)
highlights.description: Walk through the tunnel touching the 'This Is Anfield' sign. One of football's most legendary grounds.

highlights.name: Albert Dock
highlights.description: Beautifully restored Victorian dock complex with museums, restaurants, and bars.

highlights.name: Cavern Club
highlights.description: The club where the Beatles played 292 times. Still hosts live music daily.

highlights.name: Tate Liverpool
highlights.description: Home to the national collection of modern and contemporary art in the North. Free entry.

highlights.name: Liverpool Cathedral
highlights.description: The largest cathedral in Britain. The tower views are spectacular.

name: Brighton
description: London's favourite seaside escape. Bohemian vibes, the iconic Royal Pavilion, vibrant LGBTQ+ scene, and The Lanes' vintage shops and restaurants.

highlights.name: Royal Pavilion
highlights.description: An extraordinary Indo-Saracenic palace built for King George IV. Jaw-droppingly opulent.

highlights.name: The Lanes
highlights.description: A maze of narrow alleyways packed with vintage shops, jewellers, and independent boutiques.

highlights.name: Brighton Pier
highlights.description: Classic British seaside amusement pier. Fish and chips, arcades, and fairground rides.

highlights.name: North Laine
highlights.description: Brighton's bohemian quarter. Independent shops, street art, vinyl stores, and veggie cafes.

highlights.name: Brighton Beach & Seafront
highlights.description: Pebble beach with the seafront promenade. Bars, clubs, and the iconic i360 tower.

name: Stratford-upon-Avon
description: Shakespeare's birthplace. A charming Tudor market town with world-class theatre, beautiful river walks, and connections to the greatest writer in the English language.

highlights.name: Shakespeare's Birthplace
highlights.description: The house where Shakespeare was born in 1564. Beautifully preserved with costumed guides.

highlights.name: Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC)
highlights.description: See a world-class Shakespeare production at the RSC Theatre on the river.

highlights.name: Anne Hathaway's Cottage
highlights.description: The thatched cottage where Shakespeare's wife grew up. Beautiful cottage garden.

highlights.name: River Avon
highlights.description: Hire a rowing boat or take a river cruise past the theatre and the old town.

name: Scottish Highlands
description: Wild, raw, and breathtakingly beautiful. Ancient castles, misty lochs, and mountains that feel like the edge of the world. Includes Loch Ness, Glencoe, and the Isle of Skye.

highlights.name: Loch Ness
highlights.description: The legendary loch famous for its mythical monster. The ruins of Urquhart Castle on the shore are dramatic.

highlights.name: Glencoe
highlights.description: Scotland's most dramatic valley. The site of the 1692 massacre and countless films (Harry Potter, James Bond).

highlights.name: Isle of Skye
highlights.description: Fairy pools, dramatic cliffs, and otherworldly landscapes. The Old Man of Storr is iconic.

highlights.name: Eilean Donan Castle
highlights.description: Scotland's most photographed castle, on a small island where three lochs meet.

highlights.name: Ben Nevis
highlights.description: The UK's highest mountain at 1,345m. A challenging but rewarding climb.

highlights.name: Highland Whisky Distilleries
highlights.description: Tour a working distillery and taste single malts at the source.

name: Manchester
description: The birthplace of the Industrial Revolution, now a powerhouse of music, football, and culture. From Factory Records and Oasis to Old Trafford and the Etihad, Manchester pulses with energy and reinvention.

highlights.name: Old Trafford Stadium Tour (Manchester United)
highlights.description: Go behind the scenes at the Theatre of Dreams. Walk through the tunnel and sit in the dugout.

highlights.name: Etihad Stadium Tour (Manchester City)
highlights.description: Explore the home of the Premier League champions with an interactive stadium tour.

highlights.name: Northern Quarter
highlights.description: Manchester's creative heart. Street art, vinyl shops, craft beer bars, independent cafes, and live music venues.

highlights.name: Science and Industry Museum
highlights.description: Housed in the world's oldest surviving passenger railway station. Interactive exhibits on Manchester's industrial legacy. Free entry.

highlights.name: Curry Mile (Rusholme)
highlights.description: Over 70 South Asian restaurants along Wilmslow Road — one of the greatest concentrations of curry houses in Europe.

highlights.name: John Rylands Library
highlights.description: A stunning neo-Gothic library housing priceless manuscripts including a fragment of the Gospel of John from AD 200. Free entry.

name: Cardiff
description: The Welsh capital blends a 2,000-year-old castle with a modern waterfront, Victorian arcades, and the roar of rugby at Principality Stadium. Compact, friendly, and full of character.

highlights.name: Cardiff Castle
highlights.description: A Norman keep, Roman fort, and lavish Victorian Gothic interiors all in one extraordinary site in the city centre.

highlights.name: Principality Stadium
highlights.description: The home of Welsh rugby. Stadium tours available, or catch a Six Nations match for an unforgettable atmosphere.

highlights.name: Wales Millennium Centre
highlights.description: A striking arts venue in Cardiff Bay hosting opera, ballet, musicals, and concerts.

highlights.name: Cardiff Bay
highlights.description: A regenerated waterfront with restaurants, the Senedd (Welsh Parliament), and boat trips around the barrage.

highlights.name: Victorian & Edwardian Arcades
highlights.description: A network of beautiful covered shopping arcades — the largest collection in the UK. Independent shops, coffee, and Welsh cakes.

highlights.name: National Museum Cardiff
highlights.description: Impressive Impressionist art collection including Renoir and Monet, plus natural history galleries. Free entry.

name: Belfast
description: A city reborn. The Titanic Quarter, political murals, vibrant Cathedral Quarter pubs, and easy access to Game of Thrones filming locations and the Giant's Causeway make Belfast one of the UK's most exciting destinations.

highlights.name: Titanic Belfast
highlights.description: A world-class museum on the site where RMS Titanic was built. Nine interactive galleries telling the full story.

highlights.name: Political Murals & Black Cab Tour
highlights.description: See the famous murals on the Falls and Shankill roads. A poignant, essential experience guided by local drivers.

highlights.name: Cathedral Quarter
highlights.description: Belfast's cultural hub. Cobbled streets filled with pubs, live music, street art, and restaurants.

highlights.name: Giant's Causeway Day Trip
highlights.description: 40,000 interlocking basalt columns on the Antrim Coast. A UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1.5 hours from Belfast.

highlights.name: Game of Thrones Filming Locations
highlights.description: Northern Ireland was the primary filming location for the series. Visit the Dark Hedges, Castle Ward, and Cushendun Caves.

highlights.name: St George's Market
highlights.description: A Victorian covered market with local food, crafts, and live music on weekends. One of the best markets in the UK.

name: Peak District
description: England's first national park, sitting between Manchester and Sheffield. Stately homes, market towns, limestone caves, and some of the finest walking in the country across moorland and dales.

highlights.name: Chatsworth House
highlights.description: The magnificent 'Palace of the Peak' — home of the Duke and Duchess of Devonshire, with 105 acres of gardens and a famous farmyard.

highlights.name: Bakewell
highlights.description: A charming market town famous for the Bakewell pudding. Browse the Monday market and cross the medieval five-arch bridge.

highlights.name: Mam Tor & The Great Ridge
highlights.description: A spectacular ridge walk with panoramic views across the Hope Valley. Known as the 'Shivering Mountain'.

highlights.name: Castleton Caves
highlights.description: Four show caves including the Blue John Cavern, famed for its semi-precious Blue John stone found nowhere else on Earth.

highlights.name: Monsal Trail
highlights.description: A traffic-free walking and cycling trail along a former railway line through stunning limestone dales and Victorian viaducts.

highlights.name: Haddon Hall
highlights.description: A beautifully preserved medieval manor house — one of the finest examples of a fortified medieval house in England.

bestRestaurants: The Old Original Bakewell Pudding Shop

name: Norfolk & Norwich
description: Wide skies, peaceful waterways, and big sandy beaches. The Norfolk Broads offer Britain's best boating, Norwich has a fine medieval centre, and the north Norfolk coast is gloriously unspoilt.

highlights.name: Norfolk Broads
highlights.description: Britain's largest protected wetland — 125 miles of lock-free waterways. Hire a boat or kayak through reed-lined channels.

highlights.name: Norwich Cathedral
highlights.description: One of England's finest Norman cathedrals with the second-tallest spire in the country and stunning medieval cloisters.

highlights.name: Holkham Beach
highlights.description: A vast, pine-fringed sandy beach regularly voted one of the UK's best. Feels like a private paradise.

highlights.name: Sandringham Estate
highlights.description: The private country retreat of the Royal Family since 1862. Explore the house, gardens, and museum.

highlights.name: Blakeney Point Seal Colony
highlights.description: Take a boat trip to see hundreds of grey and common seals basking on the shingle spit.

highlights.name: Norwich Lanes
highlights.description: A network of medieval streets full of independent shops, cafes, and street food. Norwich's answer to The Lanes in Brighton.

name: Jurassic Coast (Dorset)
description: England's only natural UNESCO World Heritage Site, spanning 95 miles of dramatic coastline. From the iconic Durdle Door arch to fossil-rich cliffs at Lyme Regis, this is 185 million years of geological history on display.

highlights.name: Durdle Door
highlights.description: A natural limestone arch jutting into turquoise waters — one of the most photographed landmarks in England.

highlights.name: Lulworth Cove
highlights.description: A near-perfect circular cove formed by the sea breaking through Portland limestone. A geological wonder.

highlights.name: Lyme Regis & Fossil Hunting
highlights.description: The fossil capital of the UK. Walk the beach where Mary Anning made her famous discoveries and find your own ammonite.

highlights.name: South West Coast Path (Jurassic section)
highlights.description: Walk the cliff paths between Lulworth and Kimmeridge for some of England's most dramatic coastal scenery.

highlights.name: Corfe Castle
highlights.description: A dramatic ruined Norman castle perched on a hilltop above the village. One of England's most iconic ruins.

highlights.name: Old Harry Rocks
highlights.description: Towering chalk stacks at the eastern end of the Jurassic Coast. Spectacular cliff-top walk from Studland.

name: Isle of Wight
description: A miniature England off the Hampshire coast. Queen Victoria's favourite retreat, with sandy beaches, dramatic chalk cliffs at The Needles, and a famous festival scene. Just a short ferry from Portsmouth.

highlights.name: Osborne House
highlights.description: Queen Victoria's beloved seaside palace. Lavish interiors, a private beach, and the Swiss Cottage where the royal children played.

highlights.name: The Needles
highlights.description: Three iconic chalk stacks rising from the sea with a Victorian lighthouse. Take the chairlift down to Alum Bay's coloured sand cliffs.

highlights.name: Shanklin Old Village & Chine
highlights.description: A picturesque thatched village and dramatic coastal ravine with waterfalls and lush vegetation.

highlights.name: Cowes & Sailing Heritage
highlights.description: The sailing capital of the UK. Home to Cowes Week, the world's oldest and largest annual sailing regatta.

highlights.name: Carisbrooke Castle
highlights.description: A medieval castle where Charles I was imprisoned before his execution. Meet the famous donkeys that draw water from the well.

highlights.name: Isle of Wight Steam Railway
highlights.description: A heritage railway running restored Victorian and Edwardian steam trains through the island countryside.

gettingThere.from: London Waterloo to Portsmouth Harbour + ferry

name: Windsor
description: Home to the world's oldest and largest occupied castle, the historic town of Eton, and the vast Great Park. A royal day trip just 30 minutes from central London with centuries of monarchy on display.

highlights.name: Windsor Castle
highlights.description: The oldest and largest occupied castle in the world. State Apartments, St George's Chapel (where Harry and Meghan married), and Queen Mary's Dolls' House.

highlights.name: Eton College
highlights.description: The world's most famous school, founded in 1440 by Henry VI. Walking tours of the historic courtyards and chapel.

highlights.name: Windsor Great Park
highlights.description: 4,800 acres of parkland with The Long Walk, the Savill Garden, and Virginia Water lake. Free to explore.

highlights.name: Changing of the Guard
highlights.description: The ceremonial changing of the castle guard with marching bands. A quintessential royal spectacle (check schedule).

highlights.name: River Thames Boat Trip
highlights.description: Scenic boat cruises from Windsor along the Thames past Bray, Maidenhead, and the riverbank meadows.

gettingThere.from: London Paddington (change at Slough) or London Waterloo

name: Durham
description: A compact cathedral city perched above a river gorge. Durham Cathedral and Castle form a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the winding medieval streets are perfect for a short, rewarding visit.

highlights.name: Durham Cathedral
highlights.description: A masterpiece of Norman architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The cloisters were used as Hogwarts in the Harry Potter films.

highlights.name: Durham Castle
highlights.description: A Norman castle now part of Durham University. Guided tours reveal the Great Hall and the Norman Chapel.

highlights.name: River Wear Walk
highlights.description: A beautiful circular walk along the wooded river gorge surrounding the cathedral peninsula.

highlights.name: Beamish Museum
highlights.description: A world-famous open-air museum recreating life in North East England from the 1820s to the 1950s. Trams, a colliery village, and a working farm.

highlights.name: Prebends Bridge Viewpoint
highlights.description: The classic view of the cathedral above the river, painted by Turner and celebrated as one of England's finest vistas.

name: Snowdonia
description: Wales' most spectacular national park, home to Mount Snowdon, medieval castles, slate quarries, and wild mountain lakes. Adventure activities abound, from zip lines to wild swimming in the shadow of Snowdon.

highlights.name: Mount Snowdon (Yr Wyddfa)
highlights.description: The highest peak in Wales at 1,085m. Hike one of six paths to the summit, or take the Snowdon Mountain Railway.

highlights.name: Snowdon Mountain Railway
highlights.description: A heritage rack railway climbing to the summit of Snowdon. Spectacular views without the hike.

highlights.name: Zip World Penrhyn Quarry
highlights.description: The fastest zip line in the world at 100mph, set in a dramatic former slate quarry.

highlights.name: Caernarfon Castle
highlights.description: A mighty UNESCO-listed Edward I castle dominating the Menai Strait. One of the finest medieval fortresses in Europe.

highlights.name: Portmeirion
highlights.description: A fantastical Italianate village on the coast, created by architect Clough Williams-Ellis. Colourful, surreal, and unforgettable.

highlights.name: Betws-y-Coed
highlights.description: A pretty Victorian village at the gateway to Snowdonia. Waterfalls, forest walks, and excellent outdoor shops.
